name: Planning a Kitchen Layout Update: The Step-by-Step Remodel Process

step.name: Step 1: Document existing conditions and clearances
step.text: Measure your existing room dimensions, ceiling heights, window casing positions, and current appliance hookups. Note the locations of structural support posts, exterior vent runs, and plumbing stacks so you know what can move easily and what will require substantial reconfiguration.

step.name: Step 2: Draft the proposed plan and verify code clearances
step.text: Create a scaled layout showing your proposed cabinet runs, cooking surfaces, refrigeration, and sink locations. Ensure you maintain adequate walkway widths between opposing counters and confirm your island has sufficient clearance for dishwasher doors to open fully without blocking traffic.

step.name: Step 3: Secure building permits and coordinate trades
step.text: Submit separate existing and proposed drawings to your local building department covering structural wall changes, electrical additions, and plumbing relocations. Coordinate licensed specialty trades to pull the necessary trade permits for running new drain pipes, water lines, and electrical wiring.

step.name: Step 4: Execute rough-in framing, plumbing, and electrical
step.text: Open up walls, modify framing as planned, and rough in the concealed mechanical systems before any wallboard goes up. Schedule municipal rough-in inspections so inspectors can verify electrical circuits, plumbing drops, and ventilation ducting while everything remains visible.

step.name: Step 5: Hang drywall, set cabinetry, and apply final finishes
step.text: Install moisture-resistant drywall, patch walls, and set your new cabinets true and level against verified field dimensions. Once counters, tile backsplash, and appliances are installed, call for final inspections and complete touch-up trim carpentry and painting.
